reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 a numeric literal has at most one sign character, and a sign, if used, is its leftmost character (abutting the digits); an unsigned literal is nonnegative. The compiler must refuse two signs, a trailing sign, a separated sign in a literal slot (VALUE, level-88 VALUE, procedure operand, argument, subscript), and must give a signed literal its sign and an unsigned one a nonnegative value.
reader.edition-search: Grepped ArithmeticFormationRules.cs, SignedIntegerLiteral.cs, SoleOperand.cs for Edition/CobolVersion/Construct/Year: none; LiteralScreen.ScreenSign takes no edition; DataBinder's VALUE-operand arm (SignedLiteralViolation, COBOL2155) is edition-blind. The only edition-dependent behaviour met on the path is DISPLAY's own 1985 rule (a numeric DISPLAY literal must be an unsigned integer), which is a different rule.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the formation rule is the same; at 85 DISPLAY of a signed literal is refused by §1985:VI.6.10.3 SR2, a different rule
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses cover abutting/separated signs in VALUE, MOVE, ADD and relations; the probes add two signs (+-5, --5, -+3 in level-88 THRU), a trailing sign (5-, 5+), signs in an intrinsic argument and a subscript

reader.notes: The sign-formation rule is enforced edition-blind by the lexer/grammar shape plus LiteralScreen.ScreenSign and DataBinder's VALUE-operand arm; every violation probed at --std 85 is refused with a named diagnostic, and signed/unsigned literal values are right.

refuter.evidence: Probe r3a.cob (--std 85, EXIT 0): VALUE -0 and VALUE -.0 into S9V9 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE print +0.0 +0.0 (a signed zero literal is the algebraic zero, GR4); MOVE -0 TO C prints +0.0; MOVE -0.0 to edited -9.9 prints ' 0.0'; IF D < -11 with D = -12 is true; COMPUTE C = -1 - -.5 gives -0.5; ADD -5 TO G (+5) gives +0. The reader's refusal probes (two signs, trailing sign, separated sign in VALUE/88/MOVE/argument/subscript) stand. Checks: 'OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.2 SR2 ... the text is in SR2'; 'OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.2 GR4 ... the text is in GR4'. (Side note, not this rule: IF -0 = +0 with two literal operands draws only warning COBOL3146 at 85; that is a relation-condition rule outside this slice.)
